maybeboard.name: Sheoldred, Whispering One
maybeboard.why: Same 7 mana. Butchers edict is the third copy of an effect Grave Pact and Dictate of Erebos already provide; Sheoldred taxes each opponent on their own upkeep regardless, and adds free reanimation every upkeep - a second Meren with no mana value or experience limit.

swaps.why: Ramp was at 5 against a target of 10; Mesmeric Fiend returns the exiled card whenever it is sacrificed, fighting the sacrifice plan, and Plan was at 40 against 30.
Same self-mill, but on a body: a sacrifice target, a death trigger, and a creature card Meren can return at end step to mill again. Player asked for it.

The Hart sacrifices itself for two lands at mana value 3, so Meren returns it each end step for repeatable double ramp plus an experience counter and a death trigger; Naturalize duplicated Krosan Grip, Reclamation Sage, Acidic Slime and Woodfall Primus without leaving a body.

Ramp was at 7 against a target of 10 and Targeted disruption heavy at 15 against 12. Two lands from one card, a redundant Cultivate, and it fetches a Forest against green at 27 pips over 21 sources; Murder was the costliest of the unconditional creature-kill spells.

Ramp was at 8 against a target of 10 and Targeted disruption heavy at 14 against 12. At two mana it lands Meren a turn earlier and its colourless mana covers her generic cost, and it cashes itself in for a card late; Doom Blade was the weakest removal left given its nonblack restriction.

review.text:
REVIEW AFTER THE IMPROVEMENTS (five swaps).

HOW IT WINS. Theme density is 40 serving of 99 - unchanged, because three of the five cards that came in are mana, which this deck needed more than another graveyard card.

Turns 1-3. 1 card at mana value 0, 6 at 1, 16 at 2, 24 at 3, average mana value 3.06. The early game is now split between self-mill and acceleration: Stitchers Supplier, Mulch and the new Satyr Wayfinder fill the yard, while Mind Stone, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Golgari Signet and Sakura-Tribe Elder put Meren on the table a turn sooner than before. Mind Stone on turn two means a turn-three Meren.

Turns 4-6. The engine turns on, and it now has fuel. Each sacrifice feeds an experience counter, a death trigger and a body in the yard. Farhaven Elf and Burnished Hart are the new pieces that matter: both die and come back, so Merens end step produces lands as well as threats. Victimize, Dread Return, Animate Dead and Necromancy are the cash-in cards; Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat, Grave Pact and Dictate of Erebos turn every death into a loss for the table.

Turns 7 and on. 6 cards at mana value 5, 2 at 6, 2 at 7, 1 at 8. Living Death, Massacre Wurm, Moldgraf Monstrosity, Butcher of Malakir and Woodfall Primus. These arrive meaningfully earlier than before the ramp was fixed, which is the point of the change.

WHAT ENDS THE GAME. Grave Pact or Dictate of Erebos plus a repeatable outlet strips every board while Blood Artist and Zulaport Cutthroat drain; Living Death is the single swing that ends a long game. Combat is a fallback on Splinterfright and Golgari Grave-Troll, both sized off the graveyard.

CURVE AGAINST LANDS AND RAMP. This is where the deck improved most. Ramp is at 9 against a target of 10, up from 5. Lands are at 37 against a target of 38. With that support behind an average mana value of 3.06, the deck now reliably casts Meren on turn three or four and still has mana to sacrifice and recast in the same turn - the activity cost the first review flagged. Artifacts are at 6 and sorceries at 10, where they were 4 and 9. Black is at 53 pips against 24 sources and green at 28 pips against 21 sources; the pip count came down as the black removal spells left, which eases the mono-black-heavy cards slightly, while triple-green Moldgraf Monstrosity and Woodfall Primus still lean on the thinner colour.

WHEN THE COMMANDER IS ANSWERED. Unchanged and still a strength - Animate Dead, Necromancy, Victimize, Dread Return, Living Death, Moldgraf Monstrosity and Golgari Grave-Trolls dredge all function with Meren in the command zone. Marginally better than before: with Ramp at 9, recasting her through commander tax is more affordable, which is how this deck recovers.

CATEGORIES. The main finding is close to closed: Ramp at 9 against 10. Creatures are at 32, up from 30, the right direction for a deck whose commander only returns creature cards. Card advantage is still at 11 against a target of 12 and Mass disruption at 5 against 6 - both one short, and Mass disruption is the one still worth filling, since this deck wins by grinding and wants the board held still while it does. Targeted disruption came down from 16 to 13 against a target of 12, so the heaviness the first review flagged is essentially gone; what is left is all efficient. Plan is at 40 against 30, still the heaviest category, but that is where a decks identity should pool.

The two stretched counts persist. Viscera Seer counts in Card advantage but only scries, so 11 reads better than it plays. Spore Frog counts in Mass disruption as a recurrable fog, which it genuinely is with Meren, but it buys a combat step rather than answering a board.

LANDS THAT MAKE NO MANA. Still one: Evolving Wilds, which sacrifices for a basic land put onto the battlefield tapped - and puts itself in the graveyard for Life from the Loam to return.

THE CARDS THAT DO NOT SERVE THE THEME. Farhaven Elf, Kodamas Reach and Mind Stone were added knowing they do nothing with the graveyard. That was the trade: a deck with a perfect theme and five ramp pieces loses to a deck that can cast its spells.
